clue.text: Shadow a non-speaking part

parts.note: dumb is an old word for unable or unwilling to speak
a ration is one person's share or portion

explanation.surface: An actor is cast as an understudy in a walk-on role with no lines.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Shadow' looks like the verb for following an actor; here it is the definition, in its sense of a faint outline or foreshadowing.
explanation.definitionFit: A foreshadowing or faint sketch of something to come is a shadow of it; both mean an indistinct outline.

clue.text: One who runs out of breath — let escape?

indicators.note: the letters are taken out of the run of words breath, let and escape, spanning the dash

explanation.surface: A runner gasps, wondering whether to let the air go.
explanation.walkthrough: The dash is punctuation only; the answer runs across the end of 'breath', all of 'let' and the start of 'escape'.
explanation.definitionFit: A sprinter or distance runner is a sportsperson competing on the track.

clue.text: Stimulant found at university, through…

parts.note: being up means in residence at a university, as in up at Oxford
per means through or by means of, as in per post

explanation.surface: Someone finds a drug on campus, and the sentence trails into the next clue.
explanation.walkthrough: The ellipses link this to the next clue for the surface only; each answer stands alone.
explanation.definitionFit: Slang for an amphetamine or similar pep pill that lifts mood and energy.

clue.text: …support workers obtaining shots in court

parts.note: to back someone is to support them
hands are manual workers, as in farmhands

explanation.surface: Continuing the previous clue, backers and staff are bringing evidence to a trial.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Court' suggests a law court; it is a tennis court, where these strokes are played across the body.
explanation.definitionFit: Tennis strokes played with the back of the racket hand facing the ball.

clue.text: Needs to start late workers

indicators.note: starting late means the first letter is lost from the word for needs

parts.note: wants are things one needs

explanation.surface: Someone must begin their shift late.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to start late' drops the opening W of WANTS. Worker ants are the classic crossword workers.
explanation.definitionFit: Worker insects in a colony do the foraging and building, hence the standard crossword sense.

clue.text: Their sin, in other words, succeeds

indicators.note: the letters of these words are re-expressed as another word entirely

explanation.surface: Somebody else's wrongdoing, put another way, actually pays off.
explanation.walkthrough: 'succeeds' looks like 'does well'; here it means takes over from a predecessor.
explanation.definitionFit: To succeed to a title or estate is to come into it after the previous holder, as an heir does.

clue.text: Railwaymen scuffle outside tender

annotationWithheld.why: Railwaymen scuffle outside tender (5): NUR (railwaymen) is clear, but no parse of 'scuffle outside' gives the remaining SE, and no source gives the setter's reading

clue.text: Reward for an MP yet to be re-elected

indicators.note: the letters are elected again in a new arrangement, a fresh order

explanation.surface: An MP who has yet to win re-election is waiting for a payout.
explanation.walkthrough: 're-elected' reads as a political event; it tells you to rearrange AN MP YET.
explanation.definitionFit: Remuneration given for work or service is a reward for it.

clue.text: Medicine taken by wise man with slops

indicators.note: the medicine is taken in by the wise man, held inside his letters

parts.note: a sage is a wise man
a pill is a dose of medicine

explanation.surface: A guru swallows a remedy and ends up with spilt liquid.
explanation.walkthrough: 'slops' could be a verb; it is the noun, liquid spilt over.
explanation.definitionFit: Slops are liquid spilt or slopped about, the result of a spill.

clue.text: Skip the whisky — and see the children's game

parts.note: to hop is to skip or jump on one foot
Scotch is whisky distilled in Scotland

explanation.surface: Someone advises passing on the drink and watching kids play instead.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Skip' looks like 'leave out'; it is the jump.
explanation.definitionFit: A playground pastime of hopping through numbered squares chalked on the ground.

clue.text: About to work steadily for the answer

parts.note: re means about or concerning
to ply a trade is to work at it steadily

explanation.surface: Someone keeps plugging away to arrive at the solution.
explanation.definitionFit: A response to a letter or question is the answer given.

clue.text: Unsophisticated listener once your…

parts.note: an ear is the organ that listens
thy is the old form of your

explanation.surface: An old-fashioned listener addresses someone, trailing into the next clue.
explanation.walkthrough: The ellipsis joins this to the next clue only for the surface.
explanation.definitionFit: Earthy humour or people are coarse, down-to-earth and unrefined.

clue.text: …right royal staunch supporter

parts.note: true means correct or right
royal blue is a shade, so royal can stand for blue

explanation.surface: Completing the previous clue, someone is a thoroughly loyal backer of the monarchy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'right royal' looks like a phrase meaning thoroughly; split it into TRUE and BLUE (as in royal blue).
explanation.definitionFit: A true-blue person is unwaveringly loyal, especially to the Conservative cause in Britain.

clue.text: Itinerant worker chasing sin

indicators.note: the worker comes after, chasing, the word for sin

parts.note: to err is to sin or go astray
an ant is a worker insect

explanation.surface: A travelling labourer pursues wrongdoing.
explanation.definitionFit: Errant knights wandered in search of adventure, so the word means roving or travelling.

clue.text: Having no address, support diminished

parts.note: to root for a side is to support it
less means reduced or diminished

explanation.surface: A homeless person finds their help cut back.
explanation.walkthrough: 'address' suggests speaking; here it is a home address.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone without fixed ties or settled home is said to be rootless.

clue.text: Supporter breaking law in the beginning

indicators.note: the law goes in, inside the word for the beginning

parts.note: the start is the beginning

indicators.note: the word law is broken up, its letters scrambled into a new order

explanation.surface: A backer flouts the rules right from the outset.
explanation.walkthrough: 'breaking' turns LAW into LWA, and 'in' puts that inside START.
explanation.definitionFit: A stalwart is a loyal, dependable backer of a cause or team.

clue.text: City strip is cleaner

parts.note: LA is Los Angeles
to strip is to undress

explanation.surface: A town's striptease is somehow more wholesome.
explanation.walkthrough: 'cleaner' reads as a comparative adjective; it is a noun, a woman who washes clothes.
explanation.definitionFit: A washerwoman who launders clothes is a cleaner of linen.

clue.text: Tense examination of the countryside

parts.note: the past is a grammatical tense
an oral is a spoken exam

explanation.surface: A nervous inspection of the rural landscape.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Tense' looks like 'nervous'; it is the grammatical tense.
explanation.definitionFit: Pastoral describes rural life, shepherds and the countryside.

clue.text: Paper that deceives crown?

parts.note: fools means deceives, as in fools someone
a cap is a crown, as on a tooth or the top of something

explanation.surface: A newspaper tricks the monarch, perhaps.
explanation.definitionFit: A traditional large size of writing or printing sheet, named from an old watermark.

clue.text: Investments, you say in the paper, sure to change

indicators.note: the sound of the word goes inside the newspaper's initials

parts.note: FT is the Financial Times

indicators.note: say signals a word spoken, the letter that sounds like it

parts.note: the letter U is pronounced like you

indicators.note: the letters of sure are changed around

explanation.surface: Someone reads in the financial pages that a sure thing is about to shift.
explanation.walkthrough: 'say' turns YOU into the letter U, which goes inside FT; 'to change' turns SURE into URES.
explanation.definitionFit: Futures are contracts to buy commodities or assets at a set price later, a form of trading stake.

clue.text: Sure to change in case of debts pressure

indicators.note: the shuffled word sits inside the outer letters
the case of a word is its outside, its first and last letters
the letters of sure are changed around

explanation.surface: Debt collectors are sure to alter their stance under strain.
explanation.walkthrough: 'case of debts' gives D and S, the first and last letters; 'to change' makes URES from SURE, which goes inside.
explanation.definitionFit: Duress is coercion or threats forcing someone to act.

clue.text: Good people in group's division

indicators.note: the good people are placed inside the word for group

parts.note: a set is a group
men are people

explanation.surface: Decent folk sit in their own section of the club.
explanation.definitionFit: A segment is a part or section into which something is divided.

clue.text: Stir — or let tea stand?

indicators.note: stirring mixes the letters of or let tea into a new order

explanation.surface: Someone wonders whether to stir the brew or let it brew.
explanation.walkthrough: 'stand' looks like letting tea brew; it means put up with.
explanation.definitionFit: To stand something, as in I can't stand it, is to put up with it.

clue.text: Trees fall and are put back in place

indicators.note: trees that fall come down in disarray, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Felled timber is set upright again.
explanation.definitionFit: To reset is to set something again in its proper position.

clue.text: Cockney being evasive, and moving aside

indicators.note: a Cockney speaker drops the H at the start of words

parts.note: hedging means avoiding a direct answer

explanation.surface: A Londoner dodges questions while sidling out of the way.
explanation.walkthrough: COCKNEY is a London East End accent famous for dropping H, so HEDGING loses its first letter.
explanation.definitionFit: Edging means moving gradually sideways, as in edging past someone.

clue.text: State that one owned up to nothing

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral for one

indicators.note: in a down clue, up means the word is read upwards, backwards

parts.note: had means owned
O is the figure zero, nothing

explanation.surface: Someone admits they once had nothing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'up' reverses HAD to DAH; 'owned up' tempts as 'confessed'.
explanation.definitionFit: A US state in the Pacific Northwest.

clue.text: The appearance of one in pieces

indicators.note: the single letter goes inside the word for pieces

parts.note: chessmen are pieces, so men
I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: Someone looks as though they are falling apart.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in pieces' looks like 'broken'; here 'in' is the container signal and pieces are chessmen.
explanation.definitionFit: A person's mien is their look, bearing or manner.

clue.text: Cunning plans for game points?

parts.note: RU is rugby union
S, E and S are compass points, south, east, south

explanation.surface: Tactics devised to score in a sport.
explanation.definitionFit: Ruses are tricks or stratagems to deceive.

clue.text: Repeat to back row — energy and speed!

indicators.note: to back the word for row is to read it backwards

parts.note: a tier is a row, as of seats
E is the symbol for energy in physics
rate means speed

explanation.surface: Someone shouts again at those in the rear seats to show some vigour.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to back' reverses TIER, giving REIT.
explanation.definitionFit: To reiterate is to say again, over and over.

clue.text: Star spotter's latest count went wrong

indicators.note: the letters of latest count go astray, rearranged into a new order

explanation.surface: A talent agent's newest tally is off.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Star' tempts toward astronomy; here a star is a celebrity.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who searches for promising performers or athletes to sign up.
